subject: Re: [AMBER] polarizable FF in amber18 or 20

messages.author: Ray Luo
messages.body:
Vaibhav,
I can ask this. There is a new polarizable force field, polarizable
Gaussian Multipole, actively under development. The PME code
supporting this force field has been released in sander in the latest
release.
All the best,
Ray
--
Ray Luo, Ph.D.
Professor of Structural Biology/Biochemistry/Biophysics,
Chemical and Materials Physics, Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering,
Biomedical Engineering, and Materials Science and Engineering
Department of Molecular Biology and Biochemistry

Best regards.

messages.author: Ray Luo
messages.body:
Vaibhav,
Thanks a lot for your interests! So far the PME coding in AmberTools is
mostly done. There is also a py-resp project capable of electrostatic
fitting for the pGM force field. The next step is to port the AmberTools
code into Amber/CUDA so we can start serious parameterization of solvated
systems.
We'll certainly ask for community-wide beta testing once it's ready. My gut
feeling is that it's at least two years away for proteins and ligands.
All the best,
Ray
--
Ray Luo, Ph.D.
Professor of Structural Biology/Biochemistry/Biophysics,
Chemical and Materials Physics, Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering,
Biomedical Engineering, and Materials Science and Engineering
Department of Molecular Biology and Biochemistry
University of California, Irvine, CA 92697-3900

other details.

Best regards
